title: Growth Modeling with fit_bayesian_growth()
text: fit_bayesian_growth() function fits von Bertalanffy, Gompertz, Logistic growth models using Bayesian methods. central methodological feature maturity-based parameterization, derives growth coefficient \(k\) observable maturity metrics rather estimating directly.

title: Growth Modeling with fit_bayesian_growth()
text: von Bertalanffy (model = "v"): \[L(t) = L_\infty - (L_\infty - L_0) e^{-kt}\] Gompertz (model = "g"): \[L(t) = L_\infty \exp\left[-\ln\left(\frac{L_\infty}{L_0}\right) e^{-kt}\right]\] Logistic (model = "l"): \[L(t) = \frac{L_\infty}{1 + \left(\frac{L_\infty}{L_0} - 1\right) e^{-kt}}\]

title: Growth Modeling with fit_bayesian_growth()
text: Directly estimates growth coefficient \(k\):
code: library(vitalBayes) library(data.table)  # Load simulated data data(growth_data)  # Filter to non-embryos with age data gdata <- growth_data[embryo == FALSE & !is.na(age)]  # Traditional k-based von Bertalanffy growth_k <- fit_bayesian_growth(   lt      = "fl",   age     = "age",   sex     = "sex",   data    = gdata,   model   = "v",   k_based = TRUE,   CV_k    = 0.5,        # 50% CV on k prior (high uncertainty)   parallel = TRUE )  growth_k$summary(c("Linf", "L0", "k", "sigma"))

text: Derives \(k\) maturity parameters (\(L_{mat}\), \(t_{mat}\)), ensuring biological consistency. derivation differs growth model: von Bertalanffy: \[k = \frac{1}{t_{mat}} \ln\left(\frac{L_\infty - L_0}{L_\infty - L_{mat}}\right)\] Gompertz: \[k = \frac{1}{t_{mat}} \ln\left(\frac{\ln(L_\infty / L_0)}{\ln(L_\infty / L_{mat})}\right)\] Logistic: \[k = \frac{1}{t_{mat}} \ln\left(\frac{L_{mat}(L_\infty - L_0)}{L_0(L_\infty - L_{mat})}\right)\] derivation ensures growth curve passes exactly point \((t_{mat}, L_{mat})\), anchoring model observable biological milestone. maturity-based? Reduced correlation: \((L_\infty, k)\) notoriously correlated; maturity parameters break Observable anchoring: Maturity milestones fall within data range, unlike \(L_\infty\) Prior propagation: Uncertainty maturity models flows growth estimates Biological coherence: growth curve must pass \((t_{mat}, L_{mat})\) full derivation, see Maturity-Based Parameterization section Statistical Methods guide.

title: Age-Specific Natural Mortality with get_stochastic_mortality()
text: Natural mortality (\(M\)) among difficult parameters estimate fisheries science, yet profoundly influences population dynamics, sustainable harvest levels, conservation assessments. elasmobranchs, obtaining direct mortality estimates particularly challenging: long lifespans make mark-recapture studies impractical, populations often sparse reliable catch-curve analysis, absence otoliths necessitates alternative aging structures uncertainties. get_stochastic_mortality() function addresses challenge implementing three established life-history-based mortality models within Monte Carlo framework properly propagates uncertainty. function accepts either vitalBayes stanfit objects (preserving posterior correlations) manual c(mean, sd) specifications, explicit handling covariance maturity parameters. vignette covers: unified mortality framework: \(M(t) = M_\infty / G(t)\) Parameter input options: stanfit objects vs. manual specification Covariance handling maturity parameters three supported mortality models Integration survivorship simulation

title: Age-Specific Natural Mortality with get_stochastic_mortality()
text: vitalBayes mortality framework expresses age-specific Chen-Watanabe mortality : \[M(t) = \frac{M_\infty}{G(t)}\] \(M_\infty\) asymptotic mortality rate \(G(t) = L(t)/L_\infty\) relative size age \(t\).

title: Age-Specific Natural Mortality with get_stochastic_mortality()
text: asymptotic mortality rate computed using von Bertalanffy formula regardless growth model used: \[M_\infty = \frac{1}{t_{mat}} \ln\left(\frac{L_\infty - L_0}{L_\infty - L_{mat}}\right)\] provides consistent mortality anchor across growth models.

title: Age-Specific Natural Mortality with get_stochastic_mortality()
text: growth model requires \(k\) derivation: Von Bertalanffy: \[k_{VB} = \frac{1}{t_{mat}} \ln\left(\frac{L_\infty - L_0}{L_\infty - L_{mat}}\right)\] Gompertz: \[k_{Gomp} = -\frac{1}{t_{mat}} \ln\left(\frac{\ln(L_\infty / L_{mat})}{\ln(L_\infty / L_0)}\right)\] Logistic: \[k_{Log} = -\frac{1}{t_{mat}} \ln\left(\frac{L_\infty/L_{mat} - 1}{L_\infty/L_0 - 1}\right)\]

text: Elasmobranch datasets frequently unequal sample sizes sexes. imbalanced_data example dataset illustrates common scenario 150 females 34 males. title: Partial Pooling for Imbalanced Sex Ratios
text: Consider estimating parameter \(\theta\) (e.g., \(L_{50}\)) sex:

title: Partial Pooling for Imbalanced Sex Ratios
text: Assume sexes share identical parameters: \[\theta_{\text{female}} = \theta_{\text{male}} = \theta\] Problem: Ignores real biological differences sexes.

title: Partial Pooling for Imbalanced Sex Ratios
text: Estimate sex independently: \[\theta_{\text{female}} \perp \theta_{\text{male}}\] Problem: Ignores sexes species. sparse sex gets unreliable estimates.

title: Partial Pooling for Imbalanced Sex Ratios
text: Model sex-specific parameters draws common distribution: \[\theta_s \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu, \tau^2)\] \(\mu\) species-level mean \(\tau\) controls -sex variation. Key insight: model learns \(\tau\) data: sexes similar → small \(\tau\) → estimates shrink together sexes different → large \(\tau\) → estimates stay separated Sparse sex → borrows strength data-rich sex

title: Partial Pooling for Imbalanced Sex Ratios
text: numerical stability, vitalBayes uses non-centered parameterization: \[\log(\theta_s) = \mu + \tau \cdot \eta_s, \quad \eta_s \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)\] separates global mean (\(\mu\)) sex-specific deviations (\(\eta_s\)), dramatically improves MCMC sampling \(\tau\) small.

title: Partial Pooling for Imbalanced Sex Ratios
text: -sex standard deviation uses half-normal prior: \[\tau \sim \text{Half-Normal}(0, \sigma_\tau)\] \(\sigma_\tau\) set via prior_tau argument. prior: Allows \(\tau = 0\) (complete pooling) data support Permits large \(\tau\) sexes genuinely differ Avoids heavy tails half-Cauchy can cause divergences
